SUPERSEDED BY OPERATOR RULING — closing without implementing.

The operator ruled that a dedicated parent verb carrying --force is the right shape and is OUT OF SCOPE
for this session, and that the current store state is ACCEPTED so long as the affected tickets are all
closed. Filed as idea [rebar:5992-f317-e05e-42f7], which carries the full verified analysis of why no
supported reparent route exists.

The acceptance condition was checked, not assumed: of the 63 tickets whose parent was cleared, 61 are
closed. TWO were not — 437c-dd9d-9e65-46e7 (in_progress) and bf03-73bf-b66a-4c84 (open) — so those fell
outside the acceptance and were REPAIRED. Both were repairable with a plain 'rebar edit --parent' and no
force at all, because their parents (9594-1f1c-bcd1-4774 and 4804-d9eb-e682-4d9c) are themselves still
in_progress / open, so the closed-parent guard never engaged. Verified by re-reading the reduced tickets:
437c parent_id='9594-1f1c-bcd1-4774', bf03 parent_id='4804-d9eb-e682-4d9c'.

So this ticket's premise — that the repair required a new capability — held only for the 61 closed
tickets, whose state is now accepted. Nothing here is implemented and nothing is pending on it.

compiled_state.description:
# A destroyed parent edge cannot be restored: no supported route re-parents to a closed parent

## Impact, and why this is filed as a defect rather than an enhancement

The reconciler cleared the `parent_id` of 63 tickets (see 88d9-fe42-e50f-4067 for that incident).
Every prior parent is recoverable from the event log, but **rebar cannot write them back**: 61 of the
63 parents are closed, and `rebar edit <child> --parent=<closed parent>` is refused by the `--parent`
validation cascade (`_commands/composer.py:503-513`): "cannot re-parent to closed ticket '<id>'.
Reopen the parent first".

So the tool can destroy a parent edge automatically but cannot restore one, and the store has no
supported path back to a state it was previously in. That is the defect.

## All four candidate routes were checked, not assumed

* `edit --parent` is the ONLY reparent path — there is no `parent` / `move` / `reparent` command, and
  `link`/`unlink` cover the six link relations, not hierarchy.
* `edit` has NO `--force`: zero mentions in its help output, and `force` does not appear anywhere in
  `_commands/composer.py`.
* `rebar revert <ticket> <uuid>` does NOT restore state. `process_revert`
  (`reducer/_processors.py:456-488`) appends a record to `state["reverts"]`; its only state effect is
  un-archiving on REVERT-of-ARCHIVED. Reverting the offending EDIT logs the revert and leaves
  `parent_id` empty.
* `fsck-recover` is git-level dangling-write recovery, not semantic repair.
* `rebar.edit_ticket` shells out to the same CLI, so the library path hits the same guard.

## Why the documented workaround is not acceptable here

"Reopen the parent first" means, at this scale: reopen ~20 epics, re-parent their children, then
re-close each. Re-closing runs the LLM completion-verification gate (`require_completion_verification_for_close = true`)
~20 times and writes fresh STATUS + COMPLETION_VERDICT events onto already-signed closes. A single
gate failure leaves a previously-closed epic OPEN — a second visible regression introduced while
repairing the first. Rewriting the close records of 20 completed epics to work around a missing flag
is a symptom-level workaround.

## Approach

Add `--force` to `edit`, scoped to bypass **only** the closed-parent status check. Follows rebar's
existing `--force` idiom (`claim --force`, `transition --force-close`): explicit operator intent,
never implicit.

Deliberately still enforced under `--force`:
* the parent must EXIST (`resolve_ticket_id` + directory check),
* a ticket may not be its own parent,
* the cycle walk (a `--force` that could build a cycle would corrupt the hierarchy, which is a
  different and worse failure than the one being repaired),
* the `status == ""` fail-closed branch (an unverifiable parent stays refused — `--force` overrides a
  KNOWN-closed parent, never an UNKNOWN one).

Only the `status not in ("open", "in_progress")` refusal for a status that is positively known becomes
overridable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `edit --parent=<closed ticket> --force` succeeds and the child's `parent_id` is the closed
      parent, asserted on the REDUCED ticket, not on the command's exit code
- [ ] without `--force` the same command still FAILS with the existing message, so the guard is not
      weakened for ordinary use
- [ ] `--force` does NOT bypass: a non-existent parent, self-parent, a cycle, or the `status == ""`
      fail-closed branch — one test per case, each asserting the specific error
- [ ] the flag is rejected/ignored coherently when `--parent` is absent (it has no other meaning)
- [ ] `--force` usage is discoverable: it appears in `edit`'s usage/help text
- [ ] every oracle is MUTATION-CHECKED with verdicts recorded on this ticket, and the mutation set
      MUST include making the bypass UNCONDITIONAL — an unconditional bypass passes the happy-path
      oracle while silently removing the guard for every caller, so the still-refused cases are the
      oracles that protect the product
- [ ] the 63 recorded parent edges are restored and verified by re-reading the reduced tickets, with
      the count confirmed against the manifest
compiled_state.title: edit cannot restore a parent edge onto a closed parent, so a destroyed hierarchy is unrepairable
